claims.label: Pilot wave fails for collisions
claims.summary: In the discussion of de Broglie's report, Pauli objected that the pilot-wave theory could not give a satisfactory account of inelastic scattering, citing Fermi's treatment of a particle colliding with a rotator.
voice: De Broglie's scheme gives the particle a definite path, guided by the wave. Very well — then apply it to Fermi's case of a particle colliding inelastically with a rotator. Before the collision the wave is spread over all the states of the rotator; afterwards the rotator is found in one definite state. Your trajectories do not tell me how that comes about. The statistical interpretation handles it without strain.
A theory that works for one particle in a free field is not yet a theory. Show me a collision.
claims.reasoning: In a collision the guiding wave in configuration space splits into many branches; Pauli argued the particle picture gave no satisfactory account of the definite final states.
claims.exchangeNote: Discussion following de Broglie's report; de Broglie later cited Pauli's objection among his reasons for abandoning the theory.
claims.later: Bohm (1952) showed that the pilot-wave theory handles measurement and collisions consistently once the apparatus is included in the wave function; Bacciagaluppi and Valentini argue de Broglie had most of the resources for an answer.

claims.label: The p-eye and the q-eye
claims.summary: In October 1926 Pauli wrote to Heisenberg that one can look at the world with the p-eye or the q-eye, but opening both at once leads to madness — anticipating the uncertainty relations.
voice: One may look at the world with the p-eye, or with the q-eye. Open both at once and one goes wrong. I wrote as much to Heisenberg a year ago; the uncertainty relations have since made the remark precise.
The electron does not keep a position and a momentum in two pockets, waiting for us to look into both.
claims.reasoning: Position and momentum representations are complementary descriptions that cannot be simultaneously sharp.

claims.label: Statistics is the content
claims.summary: Pauli regarded the statistical interpretation as the physical content of the theory rather than a confession of ignorance.
voice: I see nothing in the experiments suggesting that the probabilities are a cover for something deeper. The statistical interpretation is not a confession of ignorance. It is the physical content of the theory, and I think we shall have to live with it.
claims.reasoning: The probabilistic predictions are complete and exact; the demand for more is not motivated by any failure of the theory.

claims.label: Waves in configuration space
claims.summary: The objection that ψ for several particles lives in multi-dimensional configuration space, not ordinary space, was widely raised against Schrödinger's realism in 1926–27. Attributing it to Pauli in this form is an inference from his general position and correspondence.
voice: Schrödinger, for one electron your wave lives in ordinary space. For two electrons it lives in six dimensions, for three in nine. What charge density is that? A wave in configuration space is not a wave in the world.
claims.reasoning: A real physical wave should propagate in three-dimensional space.
